column2: Every asset must match the approved paint-over PAINTOVER-TOWN.png (Card Game Art / Paintovers): cozy storybook architecture, painterly style matching our card art (clean bold shapes, soft cel-shaded painting, rich but harmonious colors). Open the paint-over and match its colors, materials, and level of detail.

Seamless, tileable, hand-painted game texture, viewed perfectly straight-on (orthographic, no perspective). Flat, even, neutral lighting: no cast shadows or directional highlights (the game lights it). Evenly distributed detail. Edges must match so it tiles (horizontally, vertically, or both as noted). No text. Square, 1024x1024.

A single hand-painted architectural element or detail, viewed perfectly straight-on (orthographic), centered, filling most of the canvas, with a fully transparent background (PNG with alpha). Soft painted shading but no cast shadows outside the object and no strong directional light. Crisp clean edges. No text. Size per row.

A single hand-painted tree or plant, full and lush, seen from a low camera slightly above (about 25 degrees down), painterly clumped-foliage shapes, warm sunlight from the upper left with soft painted shading inside the foliage, base/trunk at the bottom center as if growing from the ground. Fully transparent background (PNG). No ground, no cast shadow, no text. Vertical 2:3, 1024x1536.

These assets dress the first vertical slice: the main town square rebuilt to match the paint-over. Claude builds simple 3D buildings and props in the game and wraps them in these painted textures; doors, windows, and trims are placed onto walls as cutouts; trees are painted cards. Existing textures (TEX-MAT-* roofs, stone, brick, wood, thatch; TEX-TOWN-*) are reused. Save to Card Game Art / Pending Review; approved files go to Card Game Art / Approved_EnvKit.
